q-124232.name: Question 1
q-124232.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}uv \\ u+v\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-{u}^{2} \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]$
q-124232.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the cross term $uv.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ 2v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ -u+2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{1}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term ${u}^{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ only."

Question 1

Which of the following are affine transformations?

  1. T1:[uv]⟶[uvu+v]
  2. T2:[uv]⟶[v2v−u]
  3. T3:[uv]⟶[−u22u+v]
a
T1 only
b
T2 and T3 only
c
T1 and T2 only
d
T3 only
e
T2 only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

An affine transformation T:R2→R2 is a function of the form x=Au+b, where x,u, and b are column vectors in R2, and A is a 2×2 matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

  • Transformation T1 is not affine since it contains the cross term uv.

  • Transformation T2 is affine. Notice that T2 can be expressed as [xy]=[v2v−u]=[v−u+2v]+[00]=[01−12]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[00]⏟b. In fact, the transformation T1 is a linear transformation.

  • Transformation T3 is not affine since it contains the quadratic term u2.

Therefore, the correct answer is "T2 only."

q-124253.name: Question 2
q-124253.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u-1 \\ {e}^{v}\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}8u+2v+2 \\ u-2v+4\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(u+v)\end{aligned}]$
q-124253.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the exponential term ${e}^{v}.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8u+2v+2 \\ u-2v+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8u+2v \\ u-2v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is not affine since it contains the term $\operatorname{ln}⁡(u+v).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ only."

q-124240.name: Question 3
q-124240.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u(u+1) \\ v+1\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}v-2 \\ 5u-7\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-v \\ -v\end{aligned}]$
q-124240.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term ${u}^{2}.$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-2 \\ 5u-7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}v \\ 5u\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-v \\ -v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-v \\ -v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{3}$ is a linear transformation.

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ and ${T}_{3}$ only."

q-124251.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6v-4u \\ 3u+3v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4u+6v \\ 3u+3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{2}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v+9 \\ v-9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{2}$ and ${T}_{3}$ only."

  • Transformation T2 is affine. Notice that T2 can be expressed as [xy]=[8v−9u4u−v]=[−9u+8v4u−v]+[00]=[−984−1]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[00]⏟b. In fact, the transformation T2 is a linear transformation.

  • Transformation T3 is affine. Notice that T3 can be expressed as [xy]=[u−58u]=[u8u]+[−50]=[1080]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−50]⏟b.

Therefore, the correct answer is "T1, T2, and T3."

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

$$

$$

$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-3+3+0=0.
$$

q-124291.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=5u+3,\,y=7v-u
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ b & 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}c \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
q-124291.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

First, notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5u+3 \\ 7v-u\end{aligned}].
$$

Separating the constants and expressing the linear part as a product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5u+3 \\ 7v-u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5u \\ -u+7v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=5+(-1)+3=7.
$$
